description: The drift guarantee, asserted as behavior: a lib member with no baseline entry floors. `Proxy` has none — the gate could not construct a receiver to probe it — so `new Proxy(…)` is reported, and a TypeScript release landing ahead of a `@no-throw/core` release floors its newcomers the same way.

diagnostics.message: Call to `Proxy` escapes this `@nothrow` function: it is declared in a `lib.*.d.ts` the shipped standard-library baseline has no entry for, and that baseline is the only carrier able to reach one, so nothing colors it and it is assumed to throw. Your outs: bridge this call with `try`/`catch`; or, if it cannot throw, report it against the shipped standard-library baseline at https://github.com/MidnightDesign/no-throw/issues — the other three carriers are keyed by npm package name, and no key in that grammar reaches a `lib.*.d.ts` member.
